evidence.repair_success_rate_pilot: 0/3 (0%) of sampled failing trials were fixed after 1 repair turn; all 3 either introduced new distinct errors or left the original error family effectively unresolved.

syntax_error_categories.LEX_ERROR: 1 trial (svm-port-t3) produced an unexpected-character lex error, consistent with a stray character not valid under Quidra's no-backslash-escape rule.
syntax_error_categories.PARSE_ERROR: Remaining trials produced cascading PARSE_ERROR diagnostics from a single root cause (e.g. Python-style tuple default arguments, colon/brace-based class or function bodies, or malformed indentation), which the parser error-recovers from, producing many repeated downstream Expected-expression errors from that one root cause.
syntax_error_categories.RESERVED_MAIN: 6 trials (svm-spec-t1, svm-spec-t2, svm-spec-t3, svm-port-t1, gmm-spec-t1, gmm-spec-t2) used a Python/C-style top-level main()/int main() entry function; Quidra rejects main as a reserved function name (error RESERVED_MAIN). Genuine cross-language convention hallucination: the model applied the widely pretrained main() convention despite the supplied guide not licensing it and Quidra's own reserved-identifier rule forbidding it.
